Package dayplanner

package dayplanner

This is where all the classes for the DayPlanner app live.

Full documentation is available in the README.md file and it isnecessary that you read it entirely.

To build and execute the program, run the following terminal commands inorder in the root directory: 

 make jar
 java -jar bin/DayPlanner.jar

The package models scheduled activities, collects them into lists by category, accepts menu input, searches activities, and persists the lists between runs. DayPlanner is the main application class. Activity is the common activity model, with HomeActivity, SchoolActivity, and OtherActivity representing the specialized categories of activities. Other activities include a location. ActivityList stores and orders activities, while DayPlannerUtils provides utility methods.

Time represents a date and time to minute precision in YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM form. It validates calendar fields, including month lengths and leap years, and supports comparison.

Activity data is persisted in custom text format called RAS (Readable Activity Serial). The full RAS specialization is avaialble in the README.md. In a RAS list, each activity is encoded on one line with its category, title, start time, end time, optional comment, and any category-specific fields. FileUtils and Input are wrapper classes to handle text file access, and console input respectively. The Tester class provides the project's automated test cases.

Some cool special features of the program include:

  • The program remembers your name and persists it to file in addition to your lists.
  • The program splits longer methods into utility methods in order to keep the code as readable and maintainable as possible.
  • The program has an automatic makefile rule that builds a tar.gz file for submission.
  • Every method in the program is fully documented regardless of being public or private
